newsitem.title: CHINA: Property fuels 8.5 pct rise in Swire 1st-half net.
newsitem.headline: Property fuels 8.5 pct rise in Swire 1st-half net.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd posted an 8.5 percent rise in interim net profit on Thursday, fuelled by a sharp rise in property profits which the Hong Kong conglomerate said should strengthen during the second half.
Swire Pacific reported net profit of HK$3.32 billion for the first six months of the year compared with HK$3.06 billion in the same 1996 period.
Profit on the sale of development properties soared to HK$3.07 billion from HK$59 million and net rental income rose to HK$1.88 billion compared with HK$1.77 billion.

"The property division experienced further growth in rental income from its investment property portolio which was enhanced by significant profits from developments for sale," Swire Pacific said in a statement.
"The property division expects further enhancement of profits in the second half-year as a result of sales of residential development properties and growth in net rental income," it said.
Swire Pacific sold 315 apartments at its Island Place project on Hong Kong Island during the period "at appreciably higher prices than the 376 unit sales concluded in 1996."
It said the remaining 93 units at the development were expected to be sold in the second half of the year.

Swire Pacific also said it had sold 103 of the 214 completed residential units at its upmarket Floridian development on Hong Kong Island since June 30 and was likely to sell the remaining 111 units by the end of 1997.
"The second-half numbers should look very good," said Anil Daswani, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, predicting a substantial increase in development profits in the second half.
He raised his net profit forecast for the full-year to HK$8.5 billion from HK$8.46 billion.
Swire reported net profit of HK$7.65 billion in 1996.

But other divisions of the company performed poorly during the first half of 1997. Cathay Pacific Airway's Ltd reported a slump in net profit on Wednesday to HK$1.07 billion from HK$1.65 billion in the first half of 1996.

"The industries division's results in the first half of 1997 were lower than those in the first half of 1996 due to weaker results from Swire Beverages' Coca-Cola operations, and from the China operations of Crown Can Hong Kong and Carlsberg Brewery Hong Kong," Swire Pacific added.
Volume growth in Swire Beverages' Coca Cola in China was satisfactory but margins remained under pressure, it said.

The conglomerate's trading division also saw its apparel business suffer from a difficult operating environment in the United States while the motor vehicle business in Taiwan was adversely affected by unfavourable market conditions.
Swire Pacific said its marine services division reported "satisfactory growth" in profit but there was no growth in container throughput at Modern Terminals in the first half.

"It looks as though the industries and trading, other businesses ex-property, were down 60 percent year-or-year which reflects significant costs in further developing their business in China," said Mark Simpson, head of research at Schroder Securities.
He said worries about that side of the business were hurting Swire shares. The stock fell HK$3.00 to HK$72.00 on Thursday.
"The market is taking a cautious view because of the significant negative of the businesses, but property is the key and that is looking healthy going forward," Simpson said.
